title: 'When we tell them pregnancies require regular medical checkups, they scoff': Afghan women's health is put at risk by the Taliban
subhead: 'Voices of Afghan Women' (4/6). Only women can care for women, yet Afghanistan is no longer training female doctors, nurses, or midwives. As a result, women's access to healthcare is becoming increasingly difficult, sometimes with tragic consequences, and undermines their mental health, as they told our special correspondent in Kabul.

title: 'Fjord,' Palme d'Or 2026: 'Cristian Mungiu lends cinematic prestige to the fight against political correctness'
subhead: In an op-ed for Le Monde, Romanian political scientist Cristian Pirvulescu argues that by once again choosing a politically divisive subject while refusing to deliver a moral verdict, filmmaker Cristian Mungiu cultivates an ambiguity that serves reactionary circles.

title: The delicate oysters of Viktoria and Nicolas Courbin's shack in Gujan-Mestras, Gironde
subhead: 'Gourmet Kiosks' (6/6). On the Arcachon Bay, which was devastated by the major wildfire that swept through the region, La Baraque à huîtres, run by Viktoria and Nicolas Courbin, is beginning to see tourists return. Despite their financial losses, the couple remain aware of how fortunate they were not to have lost everything.

title: The Ukrainians sleeping in Kyiv's metro even on strike-less nights: 'Otherwise, you're up all night worrying'
subhead: As Russian bombings intensify and air defenses weaken, a growing number of the Ukrainian capital's residents are heading underground at nightfall as a precaution, without waiting for possible alerts.

title: Mahmoud Darwish and Tamar Ben Ami: The impossible love of a Palestinian poet and an Israeli dancer
subhead: In the early 1960s, in Haifa, Israel, the young Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish fell in love with Tamar Ben Ami, a Jewish Israeli dancer. Their romance was intense but brief. From this forbidden love, the writer composed a poignant poem, 'Rita and the Rifle,' which is still sung throughout the Arab world.

title: Why are heatwaves becoming more frequent in France?
subhead: Between May and July, France was the most abnormally hot country in the world, compared to its average heat index. While the role of global warming is not under debate, the frequency of this summer's heatwaves is a topic of scientific debate.
